snippet.title: How to Create Coupons
snippet.description:
Learn how to create and manage coupons on your site to boost sales and reward your customers!
In this video, we'll walk you through the essential steps to set up various discount types, customize your coupon rules, and promote your offers to ensure a smooth and rewarding shopping experience.
What you will learn:
Coupon Types: Discover the five different ways to offer discounts, including Fixed Discounts, % Discounts, Free Shipping, Sale Prices, and "Buy X Get Y Free" deals.
Customizing Details: Learn how to set unique coupon codes, choose eligible products or categories, and include recurring subscriptions in your offers.
Set Limitations: Master the setup of usage restrictions, such as setting specific validity dates or limiting the total number of uses per customer.
Promotion & Management: See how to track your coupons from the main dashboard and quickly promote them using email campaigns or social media templates.

In this video, we’ll guide you through the process of adding gift cards to your store, customizing their design, and tracking your sales history to provide a seamless gifting experience for your audience.
What you will learn:
Add to Site: Learn how to navigate to your catalog and use the Editor to design your gift card page and customize your navigation bar.
Customize Gift Cards: Discover how to add personalized names, descriptions, and images. You’ll also see how to set preset amounts or allow customers to enter their own custom value.
Manage Sales: Master the Gift Card Sales table to track purchase history, including codes, recipient emails, and current status.
Manual Issuing & Emails: Learn how to manually issue new gift cards to specific contacts and customize the automated emails that recipients receive.

snippet.title: How to manage your Online Store catalog
snippet.description:
Learn how to create products and manage your online store catalog to best suit your business and customers! 

In this video, we'll walk you through the essential steps to add new products, organize them into categories, and manage your inventory, ensuring a professional and streamlined shopping experience. 

What you will learn:

Create Products: Start by learning how to add a new physical product and fill in mandatory information like the product name and price. See how to speed up your workflow by using AI to generate product descriptions and images. 

Set Up Pricing & Inventory: We’ll show you how to manage your pricing details, including adding strikethrough prices for products on sale and calculating profit margins. We’ll also cover how to track inventory quantities automatically and set up pre-order options for out-of-stock items. 

Product Variants & Modifiers: Master the setup for products that come in different sizes or colors by creating product options and variants. You'll also learn how to add modifiers, which allow for customizations that don’t require inventory tracking,  like text engravings or embroidery patterns.

Manage Categories: Learn how to arrange your products inmulti-level hierarchies using categories and subcategories. We'll show you how to assign products to categories and manage their visibility on your site. 

Bulk Catalog Management: Save time by learning how to perform bulk actions, such as changing prices or ribbons for multiple items at once. Plus, see how to export your catalog to a CSV file for large-scale edits and import it back to your site instantly.

snippet.title: Step by Step: Edit Existing Orders from Your Wix Dashboard
snippet.description:
When you're running a business, there's nothing more important than giving customers the perfect experience they're expecting. snippet.title: How to Use the SEO Dashboard | SEO on Wix
snippet.description:
Wix’s SEO Dashboard puts Google Search Console data at your fingertips. Track a site’s performance on Google with integrated insights, and access Wix SEO tools and educational resources—all from one place.
Learn more:
https://www.wix.com/seo/learn/resource/seo-dashboard-search-console-data

00:00 Intro by Mordy Oberstein
00:19 Site performance over time 
01:37 Most significant pages insights
02:41 Most significant queries insights
04:14 SEO tools and settings section
04:45 SEO educational widget

With the SEO Dashboard, you can:

1. Track site traffic using Google Analytics. View changes in clicks and impressions: overall, by individual page or by query.

2. Access SEO tools, including:

• SEO Setup Checklist: Get a personalized checklist of foundational SEO tasks that you can complete right from the Dashboard.
• SEO Settings: Apply folder-level settings to meta tags, robots meta tags, structured data markup and more, or manage your page’s SEO at scale with Edit by Page. 
• URL Redirect Manager: Implement single, group, or bulk redirects.
• Site Verification: Apply meta tags to verify your site on search engines and platforms like Google, Bing, Pinterest and beyond.
• Site Inspection: Monitor the status of your pages within Google’s index.
• Sitemaps: View the individual sitemaps Wix automatically creates and optimizes for your site.
• Robots.txt Editor

3. Get relevant educational resources chosen for your particular site, on a range of topics including on-site optimization, keyword research, analytics and reporting, local SEO and more.

--

About SEO on Wix:
Wix is designed to help you manage SEO more efficiently, while giving you the freedom to customize. That means the platform automatically handles some of the more time-consuming SEO tasks for you—like creating dynamic XML sitemaps and generating various types of structured data markup—while giving you the control and flexibility to edit canonical meta tags, robots meta tags, open graph and more. Plus, you get Google Search Console integrations to let you quickly check your pages’ indexability, track changes in site traffic and more.

Learn more about Wix’s SEO capabilities here:
https://www.wix.com/seo

Wix: Built with SEO in mind.

snippet.title: Wix Sites Are Faster than Ever | Wix Performance
snippet.description:
In the last few years, we’ve made Wix websites even faster, achieving dramatic improvements for Core Web Vitals and increasing the ratio of Wix sites with good scores by over 10x. 

To make it happen, we:

• Host all our sites on a globally distributed CDN infrastructure, enabling automatic caching of all site resources, including the HTML.
• Optimize for the Largest Contentful Paint by prioritizing image and font resources, and by lazy loading elements outside the viewport.
• Automatically convert Images to WebP while resizing and cropping for optimal media delivery. 
• Compress all resources using Brotli to ensure faster downloads.
• Utilize code splitting and dynamic imports so sites load quickly regardless of complexity.
• Ensure all our components are built to minimize layout shifts, using proper dimensions, CSS aspect ratios and font preloads.
• Use Web Workers to reduce main-thread blocking JavaScript and minimize input delays for increased site responsiveness.

Learn more about Wix Performance:
https://www.wix.com/performance

--

snippet.title: Alexis Lloyd of Medium and the Evolution of Content | Now What? by Wix
snippet.description:
Alexis Lloyd leads product design at the intersection of publishing and technology and she’s spent her career working on future-forward solutions for readers to discover the content they want. Alexis is the co-founder of Ethical Futures Lab, where she aims to positively influence the future of AI and technology platforms, and she’s worked as a creative technology leader at The New York Times focused on the future of news, before joining Axios and then Automattic to transform their design practices. As VP of product design at Medium, Alexis is dedicated to the role technology can play in evolving user-centered design when it comes to the written word, and how platforms like Medium can create experiences that support interdependent systems and society as a whole. We talk to Alexis about the power and peril of the creator economy, how Medium is building relationships between readers and writers and why artificial intelligence might just supercharge human creativity.

More episodes at https://www.wix.com/nowwhat

Paul Turzio is using data to upend the prevailing wisdom about how and why customers fall in love with their favorite brands. The SVP of Data & Marketing Sciences at R/GA recently led a global survey that asked 16,000 customers about their relationships with brands. The findings and subsequent report titled The Power of Brand Relationship Design have shifted the assumptions surrounding everything from marketing technology (MarTech) to the role of personalization in turning one-time customers into loyal fans. In this episode, we talk to Paul about conducting the right experiments with MarTech, the importance of post-purchase experiences and why brands need to keep their promises to customers.

More episodes at https://www.wix.com/nowwhat

snippet.title: WarnerMedia’s Richard Jennings on Design Transformation | Now What? by Wix
snippet.description:
Richard Jennings has seen the disruptive power of technology firsthand. The veteran design leader spent much of his career in the music and media industries, where he’s watched technology change the shape of business seemingly overnight. Witnessing all the ways people consume, discover and enjoy entertainment change so rapidly has had an indelible impression on Richard –– and it shaped his approach to leading design teams at HBO and WarnerMedia. In this episode, we talk to Richard about where he finds inspiration, his work in making the design industry more inclusive and what organizational evolution looks like during a global pandemic.

More episodes at https://www.wix.com/nowwhat

snippet.title: Natalya Shelburne on the Myths of Design Engineering | Now What? by Wix
snippet.description:
Designers who code are often described as unicorns. Mythical creatures, not of this world, capable of incredible feats. Natalya Shelburne is on a mission to change all of that. She says these so-called unicorns should be as commonplace as horses. Natalya knows a lot about sitting at the intersection of art and code, she’s the co-author of the Design Engineering Handbook, the senior manager of design infrastructure at GitHub and was previously senior software engineer at The New York Times. And in this episode, Natalya breaks down the misconceptions of the design engineer, gets to the root of making designer/developer collaboration work (hint: it’s about people), shares the value of design systems for better business outcomes and offers advice on carving out a career on the multidisciplinary path.

More episodes at https://www.wix.com/nowwhat

snippet.title: Printful’s Davis Siksnans and the On-Demand Entrepreneur | Now What? by Wix
snippet.description:
The pandemic was a time of peaks and troughs for Printful, the custom printing company Davis Siksnans helped launch in 2013. His organization experienced explosive growth in both revenue and headcount during the pandemic, expanding from 500 employees in 2019 to 1,600 in 2020. But he was also forced to reckon with how his global workforce and supply chain was impacted by COVID-19 and make adjustments to help the company navigate on the fly. In this episode, we talk to Davis about running an eCommerce business during a global crisis, how Printful is making eCommerce more sustainable and the most important leadership lessons he’s learned after nearly a decade in business.

More episodes at https://www.wix.com/nowwhat

snippet.title: How to Anticipate Failure with Trevor Hubbard of Butchershop | Now What? by Wix
snippet.description:
Trevor Hubbard has spent the last decade thinking about what leads to failure. His process around identifying weak points is core to his work at Butchershop, the agency he founded in 2009. In fact, during one retreat a couple years ago, Trevor and the executive team listed out potential conditions that could lead to Butchershop’s demise. Among them? A global disaster that prevents them from leaving San Francisco or going to the office. We talk to Trevor about how moving to a distributed workforce opened the door to new business perspectives for Butchershop, the non-profit his team launched seemingly overnight at the start of COVID-19, his system for minimizing meetings, and how his process has helped many massive companies swim, rather than sink.

More episodes at https://www.wix.com/nowwhat

snippet.title: Joy Cho of Oh Joy! and Growing On Your Own Terms | Now What? by Wix
snippet.description:
Joy Cho has gone from a freelance designer sharing her inspiration to building one of the most influential brands on the planet — and she has the 15 million Pinterest followers to prove it. The founder and creative director of the lifestyle brand Oh Joy! has partnered with everyone from Target to Microsoft to Keds to create products that reflect her singular aesthetic. snippet.title: Emily Heyward of Red Antler and the Soul of a Brand | Now What? by Wix
snippet.description:
If you’ve bought from a buzzy direct-to-consumer brand in the last decade, there’s a good chance its brand was crafted by Red Antler. The Brooklyn-based agency founded by Emily Heyward, JB Osborne, and Simon Endres is the creative brain behind brands like Casper, Allbirds, and Hinge, and has defined an unmistakable millennial style through its work. But creating a breakthrough brand doesn’t stop at a snappy tagline or a perfect logo, it’s about understanding your customers at a foundational level and gaining their trust in the process. We talk to Emily about how branding has evolved since she launched Red Antler, her new book Obsessed: Building a Brand People Love from Day One, what changes the studio has gone through since COVID-19, and how working with businesses you believe in is vital to success.

  This is the second episode of Now What? A new podcast series from Wix, hosted by Rob Goodman, about how technology is changing… everything. Subscribe and follow the show for new episodes. Get show notes, subscribe to our newsletter, and learn more at https://www.wix.com/nowwhat

And today I'm going to show you how I shop online.

Using my mind.

Time to try another site.
Next.
Second try
Website number two.
Pop up. Close pop up.

Pop up.
Close website.
Third try
Oh this is a nice shirt.
I’m going to buy this one.
Buy now.
Uh oh, timed order form.
[Clock begins ticking]
I’m going to have to rush to fill this out in time. 
3… 2… 1
Aw man, time’s up.
This happens all the time.
I’m not backing down.
Last try
This website looks clear.
It’s also easy to navigate.
This is a cool shirt. 
Ok, moment of truth.
Buy now.
This form looks good.
Nice spacing, static labels.
Place order.
Mission accomplished.

snippet.title: How to Create an Admin Page to Manage Booking Requests (Part 2/2) | Velo by Wix
snippet.description:
To learn more visit:
https://www.wix.com/velo?utm_campaign=bd_youtube_velo

Learn how to use the Wix Bookings API to create your own admin page, so you can manage all your booking requests. You’ll use two repeaters to view, approve or dismiss booking requests—one for all your pending requests and the other for dismissed requests. Each repeater will be connected to its own dataset with different filter values. This ensures each dataset retrieves only the relevant data from the “Pending Appointments” collection (created in the first part of this tutorial) and populates each repeater appropriately. Then, you’ll add code that gives functionality to the elements on your admin page, like approve or dismiss booking requests, or contacting clients via email.

snippet.title: How to Create a Quick-Booking Form with the Wix Bookings API (Part 1/2) | Velo by Wix
snippet.description:
To learn more visit:
https://www.wix.com/velo?utm_campaign=bd_youtube_velo

Learn how to create a quick-booking form for your services using the Wix Bookings API. In this video, you’ll build a form that lets clients quickly book an appointment for the current week. You’ll use a lightbox, text and a variety of user input elements to create and design the form. Then, you’ll create a new collection, “Pending Appointments”, to store client info and manage the status of your booking requests (i.e. pending, approved or dismissed). You’ll add several functions to ensure that when clients make a booking request, they’ll only see available dates and times—all of your requests marked as “pending” or “approved” will be filtered out and not appear as an option in the form. When a potential client submits a booking request, all their info will appear in your “Pending Appointments” collection as a new item and their status will be labeled as “pending” until you approve or decline their request.

Check out the second video, “How to Create a an Admin Page to Manage Booking Requests”, in this two-part tutorial here:
https://youtu.be/_hKsMICCfAM
